The Importance of Nutrition During Monsoon: How to Keep Your Immune System Strong

The monsoon season brings with it a sense of relief from the scorching heat, but it also poses a significant challenge to our immune system. The increased humidity and moisture create an ideal environment for the growth of bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens, making us more susceptible to illnesses.

Understanding the Impact of Monsoon on Our Health

The monsoon season is characterized by an increase in waterborne diseases, respiratory infections, and vector-borne illnesses. The immune system plays a crucial role in protecting us against these diseases, and a well-balanced diet is essential for maintaining a strong immune system.

Nutritional Requirements During Monsoon

A healthy diet that includes a variety of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins is essential for maintaining a strong immune system. Some of the key nutrients that are essential for immune function include:

  • Vitamin C: found in citrus fruits, strawberries, and bell peppers
  • Vitamin D: found in fatty fish, egg yolks, and fortified dairy products
  • Omega-3 fatty acids: found in fatty fish, flaxseeds, and walnuts
  • Probiotics: found in yogurt, kefir, and fermented vegetables

Role of Nutrimix in Boosting Immunity

Nutrimix, a blend of sprouted ragi, sprouted jowar, sprouted green gram, roasted almonds, cashews, and cardamom, is a nutritious and healthy snack that can help boost our immune system. Q: Are there any specific nutritional supplements that I should take during the monsoon season?

Scientific References

Recipe: Nutrimix and Vegetable Porridge

Prep Time: 15 minutes

blogs.title: Ragi Revival: Harnessing the Nutritional Potential of Finger Millet in Modern Nutrition
blogs.content:
Ragi Revival: Harnessing the Nutritional Potential of Finger Millet in Modern Nutrition

Finger millet, known as ragi, has been a staple in South Indian kitchens for centuries. Its resilience in arid climates and rich nutrient profile make it a perfect fit for today’s health‑conscious consumers, especially during the monsoon when immunity‑boosting foods are in high demand. Ragi’s inclusion in Nutrimix—a blend of sprouted ragi, sprouted jowar, sprouted green gram, roasted almonds, cashews, and cardamom—offers a convenient way to harness its benefits within an everyday diet.

History

Ragi’s origins trace back to the Indus Valley Civilization, where archaeological evidence suggests cultivation as early as 2500 BCE. Ancient Ayurvedic texts describe ragi as a “medicinal grain” that supports digestion, reduces inflammation, and balances blood sugar. In rural households, it was traditionally ground into flour for flatbreads (rotis) and porridges, often cooked with spices and legumes. Over centuries, ragi’s popularity spread across the Indian subcontinent, with each region adding its own culinary twist.

Nutrition Profile

Sprouted ragi flour is a powerhouse of macro‑ and micronutrients. A 100‑gram serving provides:

  • Protein: 12 g – higher than most cereals and comparable to soy.
  • Dietary Fibre: 5 g – supports gut health and satiety.
  • Calcium: 50 mg – 5% of the daily requirement.
  • Iron: 4 mg – 22% of the daily value, aiding oxygen transport.
  • Magnesium: 90 mg – essential for enzyme function and muscle relaxation.
  • Phosphorus: 150 mg – supports bone integrity.
  • Vitamin B12: 0.6 µg – rare in plant sources, improves energy metabolism.
  • Rheumatoid arthritis‑supporting flavonoids such as quercetin.
  • Low glycaemic index (GI 46) – maintains stable blood sugar levels.

The sprouting process enhances bioavailability of these nutrients, reduces antinutrients like phytic acid, and increases antioxidant activity.

Benefits

1. Immune Support – Ragi’s high vitamin B12 content and flavonoids strengthen the immune system, making it suitable for monsoon immunity needs.
2. Digestive Health – Dietary fibre promotes regularity, while prebiotic compounds feed beneficial gut bacteria.
3. Blood Sugar Regulation – Low GI and magnesium help stabilize glucose levels, beneficial for diabetics and those seeking steady energy.
4. Bone Strength – Calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium contribute to bone density, reducing osteoporosis risk.
5. Heart Health – Dietary fibre reduces LDL cholesterol, and magnesium improves vascular tone.

Usage

Incorporating sprouted ragi into daily meals is straightforward. Nutrimix can be added to:

  • Breakfast porridges: mix 2 Tbsp of Nutrimix with hot water or low‑fat milk; add a pinch of cardamom for aroma.
  • Smoothies: blend Nutrimix with banana, spinach, and oat milk for a nutrient‑dense drink.
  • Snack bars: combine Nutrimix with dried fruits, honey, and nuts; bake at 180°C for 15 minutes.
  • Soups: stir 3 Tbsp of Nutrimix into vegetable broth; let simmer until thickened.
  • Roasted snacks: toss Nutrimix with olive oil, salt, and chili flakes; roast at 200°C for 10 minutes.

Sprouting ragi at home is simple: soak dried ragi grains overnight, rinse, and keep in a covered bowl at room temperature until sprouted (typically 48 hours). This process reduces cooking time and boosts nutrient density.

Recipes

Monsoon Ragi Ladoo
Ingredients: 1 cup Nutrimix, 1 cup desiccated coconut, 1/2 cup jaggery syrup, pinch of cardamom, sesame seeds for garnish.
Method: Heat nutmeg in a pan, add coconut and jaggery syrup; stir until syrup thickens. Mix in Nutrimix, shape into small balls, and garnish with sesame seeds.

Ragi & Almond Energy Balls
Ingredients: 1/2 cup Nutrimix, 1/ réserve de 1/4 cup roasted almonds, 1/4 cup cashews, 1 Tbsp honey, 1/2 Tbsp coconut oil.
Method: Blend nuts into fine crumbs. Ministir Nutrimix, honey, and coconut oil; combine with nuts; shape into balls.

Ragi & Green Gram Soup
Ingredients: 1 Tbsp Nutrimix, 1 cup sprouted green gram, 2 Tbsp chopped carrots, 1 Tbsp ginger, 1 Tbsp garlic, 4 քաղաքական cups vegetable stock, salt, pepper.
Method: Sauté ginger and garlic, add vegetables, stock, and green gram; simmer 15 minutes. Stir in Nutrimix, season, and serve hot.

FAQs

Q: Is sprouted ragi suitable for vegans?
A: Yes, sprouted ragi is plant‑based and free from animal products.

Q: Can ragi be consumed during pregnancy?
A: Ragi is rich in iron and calcium, beneficial for pregnant women. Consult a healthcare provider for individual needs.

Q: How does ragi compare to other millets?
A: Ragi has a higher protein and calcium content compared to pearl millet, but lower iron than foxtail millet.

Q: Is ragi gluten‑free?
A: Yes, ragi is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for celiac patients.

Q: How long does sprouted ragi stay fresh?
A: Store sprouted ragi in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

Scientific References

1. Kumar, P., et al. (2019). “Nutritional and Functional Properties of Sprouted Finger Millet.” Journal of Food Science and Technology, 56(4), 2345‑2352.
2. Sharma, S., & Singh, R. (2021). “Effect of Sprouting on Phytochemical Content of Finger Millet.” International Journal of Food Properties, 24(7), 1123‑1134.
